heroHeadline: Moldova Summons Russian Ambassador Over Transnistria Duma Polling Stations
heroSubtitle: Moldova's Foreign Ministry summoned Russian Ambassador Oleg Ozerov on September 3 and delivered a formal note of protest over Moscow's plan to open 16 additional Duma-election polling stations across Transnistria — 17 in total against the single Russian Embassy station Chisinau has authorised. The summons followed Foreign Minister Mihai Popșoi's September 2 warning that any unauthorised station would be treated as an unfriendly act, after Transnistrian leader Vadim Krasnoselsky first disclosed Moscow's plan and Chisinau's Foreign Ministry objected on August 31. Russia has given no indication it will scale back the plan ahead of the September 18-20 State Duma vote. No new Moldovan airspace breach has been confirmed since the August 30 crossing near Dnestrovsk, the longest lull in the drone crisis since it began August 9, with the crossing count holding at thirteen across eight confirmed events.
